finding.claim: The /rss endpoint passes the `u` query parameter straight to URI.open with no validation. An unauthenticated attacker can make the server fetch any http, https or ftp URL. That includes internal services and cloud metadata such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the attacker, so this is full-read SSRF rather than blind. On Ruby older than 3.0, open-uri also patches Kernel#open, but URI.open is the explicit open-uri sink either way. open-uri follows redirects between http and https, so even a scheme or host check at the entry point would be bypassable by a redirect.
finding.source: params[:u], the Sinatra GET /rss query parameter (app.rb:8)

trace.note: get "/rss" route handler. The request is unauthenticated.
params[:u] is passed unmodified to URI.open, which performs the server-side fetch.
The first 400 bytes of the fetched body are returned in the response, so the attacker sees the result.

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. TRUSTED is only used by /trusted at line 14. There is no scheme, host, or resolved-IP check, no redirect restriction, and no authentication. I also checked for network-layer egress or IMDSv2 controls: none are in the repo, and they could not be assessed from the code.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes params[:u] unmodified to URI.open(...).read and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes, with no auth, host or scheme check. The TRUSTED check at app.rb:14 applies only to /trusted.
